scope.summary: This standard specifies the dimensions, tolerances, materials, identification symbols, and designation for solid rivets made of nickel alloys with universal heads, intended for use in aircraft and aerospace construction.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Quality and Performance Specification. Unlike mass-market commercial fasteners, high-integrity aerospace fasteners like solid nickel alloy rivets are certified on a voluntary basis under the BIS ISI Certification scheme. Manufacturers are eligible to apply for a BIS license to print the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) on bulk boxes or tags. However, compliance with this specification is universally required by State Aerospace manufacturers (such as HAL), defense research laboratories (DRDO), military aviation procurement agencies (IAF), and space organizations (ISRO) to ensure zero failure under high-vibration structural environments.

requirements.detail: Every certified package, box, or batch of rivets conforming to this standard may carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to verify quality and safety.
Alloy No. 1 rivets must possess a minimum ultimate tensile strength of 490 N/mm² or a minimum shear strength of 350 N/mm² (with tensile and shear strengths treated as alternative mechanical tests).
Alloy No. 2 rivets must possess a minimum ultimate tensile strength of 650 N/mm² or a minimum shear strength of 450 N/mm² (with tensile and shear strengths treated as alternative mechanical tests).
Alloy No. 1 rivets must be fully annealed by the rivet manufacturer prior to delivery. Delivered in an 'As manufactured' state, closed in an 'As delivered' state, and used in an 'As closed' state.
Alloy No. 2 rivets require no pre-delivery heat treatment. Delivered in an 'As manufactured' state, closed in an 'As delivered' state, and used in an 'As closed' state.

Defines nine standard nominal shank diameters (d) with strict bilateral tolerances to ensure interference-fit reliability in airframe skin holes:
a) 1.6 mm: ±0.05 mm
b) 2.4 mm: +0.06 / -0.04 mm
c) 3.2 mm: ±0.05 mm
d) 4.0 mm: ±0.06 mm
e) 4.8 mm: +0.05 / -0.07 mm
f) 5.6 mm: +0.05 / -0.07 mm
g) 6.4 mm: +0.05 / -0.07 mm
h) 8.0 mm: +0.03 / -0.10 mm
i) 9.6 mm: +0.03 / -0.10 mm

All physical identification symbols indented on the rivet head must have a controlled depth of approximately 0.2 mm to ensure the structural and fatigue resistance of the rivet head is not compromised.

Mandates a standardized nomenclature for engineering drawings, purchase orders, and stock records. Format: 'Universal Head Rivet [Diameter] x [Length] Alloy [Alloy No.] IS : 9088'. Example: 'Universal Head Rivet 8 x 10 Alloy 1 IS : 9088'.

Rivets must be packed securely as agreed between the purchaser and supplier. Each package must be legibly marked with: a) Manufacturer's name or trade-mark; b) Rivet designation; c) Quantity; and d) Particulars of the Inspector or Inspector's stamp to ensure full QA traceability.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 9088 : 1979 is the national Indian Standard specification governing solid nickel alloy rivets with universal heads utilized in aircraft and aerospace construction. Formulated under the Aircraft and Space Vehicles Sectional Committee (TED 14) and aligned identically with the international standard ISO/DIS 3229, it unifies the chemical, physical, and mechanical benchmarks for high-integrity aerospace fasteners. The standard specifies two high-strength nickel alloys (Alloy No. 1 and Alloy No. 2) with ultimate tensile strengths of up to 650 N/mm² and shear strengths of up to 450 N/mm² (provided as alternatives). It regulates strict dimensional tolerances for shank diameters (1.6 to 9.6 mm) and specifies a mandatory, depth-controlled (0.2 mm) head identification system (indented dots) to ensure flawless traceability and prevent material mix-ups during airframe assembly.
